summary: Colville tribal-land tower built 1936 with an L-4 living cab; staffed into 1938, then abandoned. The steel tower stands; the cab is gone.

facts.design: 54 ft steel International Derrick tower; its L-4 living cab was destroyed

access.note: On Colville Confederated Tribal land. No trail or road leads to the tower, and non-tribal visitors must buy a recreation permit; check with the tribes before any trip.

visit.trail_note: No trail or road leads to the tower; TrailChick describes BIA roads, cross-country travel through fireweed, and a round trip of about 5.6 miles.

corrections.proposed: 54 ft steel International Derrick tower; the L-4 was the living cab, since destroyed
corrections.why: The register and TrailChick describe a 54 ft steel International Derrick tower with an L-4 cab for living quarters. The cab was destroyed, and the tower still stands, so the record's design field names only the cab.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and TrailChick say a fallen tree destroyed the L-4 cab; firelookout.com and willhiteweb.com say a falling snag did. The story reports both causes.

notes_for_editor: Core facts (1936 build, L-4 cab, staffed into 1938, abandoned, standing) agree across four sources. Access level 'permission' rests on the Colville tribal-land permit note, which appears on TrailChick's Strawberry and Whitestone Ridge pages, not on a Strawberry-specific rule; verify with the Colville Confederated Tribes before relying on it. Record elevation 1786.4 m is close to TrailChick's 5,863 ft (about 1,787 m); left unchanged. A 1934 newspaper item quoted on washingtonlookouts.weebly.com/strawberry-mountain1.html refers to a 'Strawberry Mountain' listed under the Colville National Forest (39N-30E-33), a different site, so it was not used. The 1938 abandonment year is an approximation: sources say the tower was abandoned after staffing into 1938.
